enzyme_name: stizolobinate synthase (L-DOPA 2,3-extradiol dioxygenase, EC 1.13.11.30) enzyme system; the separate ring-closure/oxidation step is unassigned
organism_context: Stizolobium (Mucuna) hassjoo and other Fabaceae; homologous DOPA extradiol-cleavage chemistry occurs in Amanita (muscaflavin) and Streptomyces lincolnensis (LmbB1)
rationale: MetaCyc splits the overall stizolobinate synthase conversion of L-DOPA into cleavage and cyclization halves, and no protein has ever been assigned to this second half; Saito and Komamine could only demonstrate a crude seedling 'enzyme system(s)', and Novotna et al. explicitly leave open whether the analogous cyclization is enzyme-catalysed or spontaneous. Calling the catalyst mono- vs bifunctional is therefore not possible.
direction_note: Closure of the muconate semialdehyde to the 2H-pyran-2-one is an oxidation that Saito and Komamine showed requires NAD(P)+; with only 2 H+ written as the acceptor the equation's free energy is meaningless, while the biosynthetic flow is unambiguously semialdehyde -> stizolobinate.

enzyme_name: stizolobate synthase (L-DOPA 4,5-extradiol dioxygenase, EC 1.13.11.29) enzyme system; the separate ring-closure/oxidation step is unassigned
organism_context: Stizolobium (Mucuna) hassjoo and other Fabaceae
rationale: Same situation as the stizolobinate branch: the only evidence is a crude plant enzyme preparation converting L-DOPA to stizolobic acid, and MetaCyc's split of that overall reaction leaves this cyclization/oxidation step without an assigned protein, so its domain architecture cannot be judged.
direction_note: The NAD(P)+ that oxidises the semialdehyde during ring closure is missing and replaced by bare protons, so ModelSEED's reverse call rests on an electron-unbalanced equation; biosynthesis runs semialdehyde -> stizolobate.

enzyme_name: no single enzyme; the conversion of the LmbB1 cyclization product toward 4-propyl-L-proline needs LmbW (SAM C-methyltransferase), LmbX (isomerase) and LmbY (F420H2-dependent reductase)
organism_context: Streptomyces lincolnensis, 4-propyl-L-proline (PPL) branch of lincomycin A biosynthesis
rationale: The substrate 4-(3-carboxy-3-oxo-propenyl)-2,3-dihydro-1H-pyrrole-2-carboxylate is the characterised LmbB1 extradiol-cleavage/cyclization product, but reaching 1,2,3,6-tetradehydro-propylproline requires methylation, isomerization, reduction and loss of the oxo-carboxylate across several Lmb proteins, so no one enzyme catalyses this entry.
direction_note: Several steps are collapsed into one entry and the ModelSEED formulas do not even balance (C9H8NO5 -> C7H9NO2), but the pathway flow is from the DOPA-derived pyrroline toward the propylproline moiety, i.e. left-to-right as written.

enzyme_name: dTDP-4-keto-2,6-dideoxyhexose 3-C-methyltransferase (TylC3 / EryBIII / AviG1 family)
organism_context: Streptomyces fradiae (tylosin), Saccharopolyspora erythraea (erythromycin/mycarose), Streptomyces viridochromogenes (avilamycin)
rationale: The dTDP-sugar C-3 branching methyl in mycarose/mycaminose pathways is installed by a stand-alone class-I SAM-dependent C-methyltransferase; aviG1 complements an eryBIII mutant, showing these are single-activity methyltransferases with no second catalytic domain.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way, so the methylating (left-to-right) direction is correct; the dGPredictor value driving ModelSEED's reverse call is a prediction artefact on a bulky dTDP-sugar.

enzyme_name: unidentified; the steps between 4-hydroxy-3-solanylbenzoate (made by the solanesyltransferase Slr0926) and 2-methyl-6-solanyl-1,4-benzoquinol are uncharacterised
organism_context: Synechocystis sp. PCC6803 and other cyanobacteria (plastoquinol-9 biosynthesis II)
rationale: Sadre et al. established 4-hydroxybenzoate as the aromatic precursor and identified only the prenyltransferase; the downstream decarboxylation, ring hydroxylation and C-methylation that this entry lumps together have no assigned proteins, so there is no enzyme whose functionality can be judged.
direction_note: The entry collapses a carboxyl-to-methyl conversion (a 4-electron reduction) plus a ring hydroxylation into one step balanced only by 5 bare protons, so no direction is thermodynamically meaningful; biosynthetically the flux runs from the prenylated hydroxybenzoate toward the benzoquinol.

enzyme_name: GlgE, alpha-maltose-1-phosphate:(1->4)-alpha-D-glucan 4-alpha-D-maltosyltransferase (EC 2.4.99.16)
organism_context: Mycobacterium tuberculosis/smegmatis, Streptomyces, and other actinobacteria; GlgE pathway of alpha-glucan synthesis
rationale: GlgE is a GH13-fold maltosyltransferase that performs one catalytic activity, transfer of a maltosyl unit from alpha-maltose-1-phosphate to the non-reducing end of an alpha-1,4-glucan; it is a homodimer, which is quaternary structure rather than a second activity.
direction_note: The alpha-glucan acceptor and the extended glucan product have been dropped, leaving 'maltose-1-phosphate <=> phosphate', so the computed free energies are meaningless; physiologically GlgE consumes maltose-1-phosphate and releases phosphate, i.e. the left-to-right direction.

enzyme_name: unidentified 2,3,6-trihydroxypyridine ring-cleaving hydrolase of the nicotine pyridine pathway
organism_context: Paenarthrobacter (Arthrobacter) nicotinovorans pAO1, pyridine pathway of nicotine catabolism
rationale: The upstream 2,6-dihydroxypyridine 3-monooxygenase is well characterised, but the enzyme that opens the resulting 2,3,6-trihydroxypyridine ring to 2-oxoglutaramate has never been purified or assigned a gene (the trihydroxypyridine mostly autoxidises to nicotine blue in vitro), so no functionality call is possible.
direction_note: Hydrolytic ring opening of an aromatic trihydroxypyridine is catabolic and effectively irreversible; re-aromatising 2-oxoglutaramate back into the ring does not occur, so ModelSEED's reverse call is biologically backwards.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (non-enzymatic) hydration/ring opening of the cyclic imine N-methylmyosmine to pseudooxynicotine
organism_context: Pseudomonas putida S16, Ochrobactrum sp. SJY1 and other nicotine degraders (pyrrolidine pathway), downstream of NicA2 nicotine oxidoreductase
rationale: NicA2 oxidises nicotine to N-methylmyosmine, which then hydrolyses spontaneously in water to pseudooxynicotine; no protein catalyses this step, so there is no enzyme to classify.
direction_note: MetaCyc carries this as a spontaneous step; imine hydrolysis to the open-chain aminoketone is essentially irreversible in aqueous solution, so the left-to-right (hydrolytic) direction is right and no enzymology supports ModelSEED's reverse.

enzyme_name: TobZ, kanamycin B / tobramycin 6''-O-carbamoyltransferase (class III carbamoyltransferase)
distinct_activities: O-carbamoyl transfer from carbamoyl-AMP to the 6''-OH of the aminoglycoside (EC 2.1.3.-)
organism_context: Streptoalloteichus (Streptomyces) tenebrarius, nebramycin complex biosynthesis
rationale: The TobZ crystal structure shows a monomeric single chain with two catalytic domains that run two chemically distinct nucleophilic half-reactions - ATP-dependent activation of carbamoyl phosphate to carbamoyl-AMP, then carbamoyl transfer to the sugar hydroxyl; this is a fused two-domain catalyst, not a multi-subunit complex.
direction_note: The ATP/Mg2+ and the AMP + PPi products of the adenylation half-reaction - the very things that make carbamoylation irreversible - are absent from the ModelSEED equation, which leaves only a carbamoyl-phosphate/phosphate exchange and invites the spurious reverse call.

enzyme_name: TobZ, tobramycin 6''-O-carbamoyltransferase (class III carbamoyltransferase)
distinct_activities: O-carbamoyl transfer from carbamoyl-AMP to the 6''-OH of tobramycin (EC 2.1.3.-)
organism_context: Streptoalloteichus (Streptomyces) tenebrarius; the same TobZ protein carbamoylates both kanamycin B and tobramycin
rationale: Same enzyme as for the kanamycin B substrate: a monomeric two-catalytic-domain chain that first makes carbamoyl-AMP from carbamoyl phosphate and ATP and then transfers the carbamoyl group to the 6''-hydroxyl, giving carbamoyltobramycin (nebramycin factor 5').
direction_note: With ATP hydrolysis omitted the equation is a near-isoenergetic carbamoyl/phosphate swap; the real enzyme is pulled forward by adenylate formation, so the carbamoylating (left-to-right) direction is the physiological one.

enzyme_name: GenK, cobalamin-dependent radical SAM C-6' methyltransferase (gentamicin X2 -> G418)
organism_context: Micromonospora echinospora, gentamicin biosynthesis
rationale: GenK carries one catalytic activity, methylation of the unactivated C-6' carbon of gentamicin X2 with retention of configuration, using a [4Fe-4S] radical SAM centre plus methylcobalamin; it has no second catalytic domain.
direction_note: GenK is not a classical SAM/SAH methyltransferase: it cleaves SAM to 5'-deoxyadenosine plus methionine and takes the methyl from methylcobalamin, so the SAM -> SAH pair written here misstates the stoichiometry (and the radical chemistry makes the reaction strictly one-way toward G418).

enzyme_name: glycine/sarcosine N-methyltransferase (GSMT, EC 2.1.1.156)
organism_context: Methanohalophilus portucalensis (MpGSMT), Aphanothece halophytica, Halorhodospira halochloris; first step of de novo glycine betaine synthesis
rationale: The MpGSMT crystal structure shows a single SAM-binding methyltransferase active site that methylates both glycine and sarcosine; accepting two successive substrates in one site is broad specificity, not a second catalytic activity (the third methylation is done by a separate SDMT protein).
direction_note: The doubled 2 SAM -> 2 SAH stoichiometry is two turnovers of one enzyme rather than a lumping artefact, and SAM-dependent N-methylation is physiologically irreversible toward dimethylglycine.

enzyme_name: LigM, tetrahydrofolate-dependent vanillate/3-O-methylgallate O-demethylase
organism_context: Sphingobium (Sphingomonas) sp. SYK-6, lignin-derived aromatic catabolism
rationale: LigM is a single-polypeptide THF-dependent methyltransferase that transfers the aryl methyl group of vanillate (or syringate) directly onto tetrahydrofolate; unlike the three-component Rieske O-demethylases it needs no partner proteins and carries only this one activity.
direction_note: LigM is a catabolic demethylase: the flux is vanillate + THF -> protocatechuate + 5-methyl-THF (left to right), and ModelSEED's reverse would have the organism methylating protocatechuate, which LigM does not do in vivo.

enzyme_name: CYP81F indole glucosinolate 4-hydroxylase (indol-3-ylmethylglucosinolate hydroxylase)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana and Brassica rapa ssp. chinensis; indole glucosinolate modification en route to 4-methoxyglucobrassicin
rationale: The 4-hydroxylation of glucobrassicin is carried out by CYP81F-clade cytochrome P450 monooxygenases, which have one catalytic activity (regioselective aromatic hydroxylation); hydroxylating at C-4 or C-1 depending on the isoform is regioselectivity, not bifunctionality.
direction_note: A P450 monooxygenation has been written as a bare isomerisation with O2 and NADPH/P450-reductase dropped; once the O2-coupled chemistry is restored the reaction is irreversible toward 4-hydroxyglucobrassicin, matching the LLM call.

enzyme_name: carbon disulfide hydrolase (CS2 hydrolase, EC 4.4.1.27), a beta-carbonic-anhydrase-family enzyme
organism_context: Acidianus sp. A1-3 (catenane form) and Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans strains S1p, G8
rationale: Smeulders et al. purified these enzymes and showed they convert CS2 (and COS) with water to H2S and CO2 but, unlike true beta-carbonic anhydrases, do not hydrate CO2 - so the CA-like fold carries only the hydrolase activity, and the octamer/hexadecamer state is quaternary structure, not a second function.
direction_note: The enzyme is a degradative hydrolase on a volatile substrate (H2S and COS escape the cell), so it runs CS2 + H2O -> COS + H2S; synthesising CS2 from COS and sulfide is not a biological reaction.

enzyme_name: isatin hydrolase (EC 3.5.2.20), a Mn(II)-dependent metallohydrolase of the kynurenine formamidase fold
organism_context: Labrenzia aggregata (isoforms a/b) and prokaryotic orthologues including human gut bacteria; indole-3-acetate/indole degradation
rationale: The crystal structures show a single metal-dependent active site that performs one reaction, amide-bond hydrolysis of isatin to isatinate (alpha-aminophenylglyoxylate); no second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: Hydrolytic ring opening of the isatin lactam is strongly favoured and catabolic; the enzyme never runs the lactamisation direction that ModelSEED recommends.

enzyme_name: medicarpin 3-O-glucoside (medicocarpin) beta-glucosidase, a plant GH1 family beta-glucosidase
organism_context: Medicago sativa / Medicago truncatula roots; isoflavonoid phytoalexin conjugate turnover
rationale: No specific gene has been assigned to medicocarpin hydrolysis; the activity is attributed to plant GH1 beta-glucosidases, which are single-domain, single-activity glycoside hydrolases (broad aglycone specificity is not a second catalytic function). Enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry and pathway rather than confirmed.
direction_note: The 'conjugate interconversion' in planta is run by two different enzymes - a UDP-glucose glucosyltransferase forward and a beta-glucosidase back - so the glucosidase itself runs only hydrolytically, toward free medicarpin.

enzyme_name: CYP710A sterol C-22 desaturase (cytochrome P450)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana (CYP710A1/A2) and tomato (CYP710A11); CYP710A2 makes brassicasterol/crinosterol from (24-epi-)campesterol
rationale: The campesterol/crinosterol pair differs only by the C-22 double bond, and the enzyme that installs it in plants is the CYP710A P450 C-22 desaturase - a single-activity microsomal monooxygenase; no NAD(P)H-linked sterol Delta-22 reductase has been characterised in plants.
direction_note: The real reaction is an O2- and NADPH-consuming P450 desaturation running campesterol -> crinosterol; MetaCyc/ModelSEED encoded it as an NADP+/NADPH dehydrogenation, and that mis-encoded redox pair is what makes the reduction direction look favourable and produced the reverse recommendation.

enzyme_name: (-)-maackiain 3-O-glucoside (trifolirhizin) beta-glucosidase, a plant GH1 family beta-glucosidase
organism_context: Cicer arietinum / Trifolium / Medicago; pterocarpan phytoalexin conjugate turnover
rationale: As for medicocarpin, the trifolirhizin-hydrolysing activity has not been assigned to a cloned gene; it is attributed to plant GH1 beta-glucosidases, which carry one glycoside-hydrolase activity per chain. Identity inferred from chemistry, not confirmed.
direction_note: Glucoside hydrolysis releasing free maackiain is the direction a beta-glucosidase runs; re-glucosylation in planta is done by a separate UDP-glucose glucosyltransferase, so ModelSEED's reverse call has no enzymatic backing.

enzyme_name: cytokinin oxidase/dehydrogenase (CKX, EC 1.5.99.12), FAD-dependent flavoprotein
organism_context: Zea mays (ZmCKX1), Arabidopsis thaliana AtCKX family, also bacterial homologues; cytokinin degradation
rationale: CKX is a single-activity FAD flavoprotein that cleaves the N6-side chain of isopentenyl-type cytokinins; the 'oxidase/dehydrogenase' double name reflects which external electron acceptor it uses (quinone preferred over O2), not two catalytic activities.
direction_note: The flavin in CKX is covalently bound and is reoxidised by an external quinone acceptor; writing free FAD/FADH2 as a soluble redox couple distorts the energetics, but the enzymology is unambiguous - CKX destroys isopentenyladenosine to adenosine plus the prenyl aldehyde, i.e. left to right as written.

enzyme_name: cytokinin oxidase/dehydrogenase (CKX, EC 1.5.99.12) acting on trans-zeatin riboside
organism_context: Zea mays and Arabidopsis CKX isoforms; trans-zeatin riboside is a preferred substrate of several CKX isoforms
rationale: Same single-activity FAD flavoprotein as for the isopentenyladenosine substrate - differing substrate preference among CKX isoforms is specificity, not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for the covalently bound flavin plus an external quinone acceptor; the physiological reaction is irreversible degradation of trans-zeatin riboside, so the LLM direction is right.

enzyme_name: unidentified isomerase of the solanaceous sesquiterpenoid phytoalexin pathway (15-hydroxysolavetivone -> 2-dehydrolubimin)
organism_context: Solanum tuberosum / Capsicum / Nicotiana, PWY-2961 sesquiterpenoid phytoalexin (lubimin, rishitin) biosynthesis
rationale: Only the upstream sesquiterpene cyclase (vetispiradiene synthase) and a pathogen detoxifying P450 are characterised in this pathway; the post-cyclase tailoring steps, including this C15H22O2 -> C15H22O2 rearrangement, have no assigned protein and may even be partly non-enzymatic.
direction_note: The pathway flux in elicited potato runs solavetivone -> 15-hydroxysolavetivone -> 2-dehydrolubimin -> lubimin, i.e. left to right as written; the direction rests on pathway orientation rather than on characterised enzymology.

enzyme_name: unidentified NAD(P)H-dependent reductase of the solanaceous phytoalexin pathway (2-dehydrolubimin -> lubimin)
organism_context: Solanum tuberosum and related Solanaceae, PWY-2961 sesquiterpenoid phytoalexin biosynthesis
rationale: Lubimin is a well-documented potato phytoalexin and 2-dehydrolubimin its proposed immediate precursor, but no gene or purified protein has been assigned to this reduction, so the catalyst's domain architecture is unknown.
direction_note: A two-electron reduction (C15H22O2 -> C15H24O2) is balanced here by two bare protons with no NAD(P)H, so the computed free energy is meaningless; phytoalexin accumulation runs toward lubimin, matching the LLM direction.

enzyme_name: unidentified oxidoreductase interconverting 3-hydroxylubimin (oxylubimin) and 3-hydroxy-15-dihydrolubimin
organism_context: Solanum tuberosum, PWY-2961 sesquiterpenoid phytoalexin biosynthesis en route to rishitin
rationale: No protein has been assigned to the C-15 aldehyde/alcohol interconversion in the lubimin-to-rishitin branch; both the aldehyde and the 15-dihydro alcohol accumulate in elicited tubers, so even the physiological direction is not established.
direction_note: The missing NAD(P)H means the direction is set by the unknown enzyme's cofactor and by pool sizes, not by this equation; both 3-hydroxylubimin and its 15-dihydro form are observed in planta, so neither the ModelSEED nor the LLM call can be supported.

enzyme_name: S-adenosyl-L-methionine:ethanolamine/N-methylethanolamine N-methyltransferase (free-base route); gene unassigned
organism_context: Ricinus communis endosperm and spinach (free-base choline synthesis, PWY-3542); distinct from the cloned phospho-base enzymes PEAMT/NMT1-3
rationale: A SAM:ethanolamine N-methyltransferase activity on free bases has been demonstrated in plant extracts, but no gene product has been assigned to it, so its domain architecture cannot be judged; the cloned plant enzymes (PEAMT/NMT) carry tandem methyltransferase domains but act on phospho-bases, not the free bases in this reaction.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation of an amine is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way toward the more methylated base (choline synthesis), so the methylating left-to-right direction is correct regardless of which protein runs it.
